sources.title: Constraints on the spectral index for the inflation models in string landscape

evidence.text: How does the canonical inflaton trajectory determine the inflationary expansion? The paper uses a spatially flat homogeneous background and counts e-folds backward from the end of inflation, with a monotonic field trajectory.

sources.title: A note on Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: How do the potential slope and canonical field displacement relate to inflationary expansion? The baseline is a single canonical inflaton background, with kinetic slow-roll parameter εH and potential approximation εV.

sources.title: Trans-Planckian censorship conjecture from the swampland distance conjecture

evidence.text: How does a scalar-field excursion translate into accumulated expansion? The paper uses d-dimensional Friedmann evolution and, for a positive potential, a slow-roll relation between the potential slope and the scalar velocity.

sources.title: S-dual inflation and the string swampland

evidence.text: How much accelerated expansion does a canonical scalar produce before inflation ends? Exact background evolution depends on both the potential and initial velocity.

sources.title: On the Field Excursion Bound

evidence.text: What enforces the flat FRW scalar field excursion bound, when can it saturate, and how robust is it to inflationary fluctuations, higher-derivative kinetics and spatial curvature?

sources.title: Constraints on the spectral index for the inflation models in string landscape

evidence.text: Integrate the proposed trajectory, restrict its parameters, differentiate to reconstruct η and ξ, and evaluate the spectral formulas. Keep the trajectory family, endpoint prescription and slow-roll truncation explicit when comparing resulting bounds.

sources.title: A note on Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: Let a light spectator field shift the inflaton value at which inflation ends. Convert the induced shift of the end surface into a perturbation of local inflationary duration and hence into curvature.

sources.title: Trans-Planckian censorship conjecture from the swampland distance conjecture

evidence.text: Estimate tower entropy using a covariant bound and invert the de Sitter entropy–potential relation. This prior argument discards additional field dependence and, in its original form, assumes strictly increasing entropy.

sources.title: S-dual inflation and the string swampland

evidence.text: Select shape and branch, solve the endpoint, displace backward to horizon exit, and evaluate observables and expansion.

sources.title: On the Field Excursion Bound

evidence.text: Appendix A gives a second higher-derivative derivation using Raychaudhuri focusing, an affinely parametrized null congruence, the Einstein equations and minimization of an auxiliary expression before integration.

sources.title: A note on Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: Specify a canonical slow-roll history and its interval, integrate the field displacement per e-fold, and compare the resulting dimensionless excursion with the proposed range cap. A local power-law estimate alone does not determine the total excursion.

sources.title: Non-canonical kinetic structures in the swampland

evidence.text: DBI supplies a motivated example in which a relativistic speed limit permits inflation on potentials too steep for canonical slow roll. The paper tests the associated potential-gradient estimate.

sources.title: Two-field inflationary model and swampland de Sitter conjecture

evidence.text: The setting describes inflation driven by the combined energy of two canonical scalar fields. A flat FRW background reduces the gravitational dynamics to relations between H, the total scalar kinetic energy and the potential.

sources.title: Non-canonical kinetic structures in the swampland

evidence.text: Small ε describes quasi-de Sitter expansion, while small η permits persistent inflation. These conditions constrain the expansion history without requiring a shallow potential or automatically negligible scalar acceleration.

sources.title: Warm tachyon inflation and swampland criteria

evidence.text: Test selected trajectories against conjectural excursion and slope inequalities, while distinguishing the tachyon coordinate from the canonically normalized scalar in the reviewed cold-inflation comparison.

sources.title: A Tip for Landscape Riders: Multi-Field Inflation Can Fulfill the Swampland Distance Conjecture

evidence.text: How does the length of a constant-latitude field trajectory compare with geodesic separation when both connect the same angular endpoints? The comparison holds the endpoint latitude fixed while varying the angular excursion.

sources.title: Bounding field excursions along null geodesics with applications to cosmology

evidence.text: How does gravitational focusing constrain scalar displacement along null geodesics, and what does this imply for inflationary field ranges, landscape exploration, and possible semiclassical extensions?

sources.title: Primordial Gravitational Waves and the Swampland

evidence.text: The analyzed inflationary regime has one canonical light field and uses potential slow-roll parameters to relate quantum-gravity inequalities to tensor production. Monotonic growth of ε lets a lower instantaneous field speed constrain the total field excursion.

sources.title: Assisted inflation

evidence.text: Can multiple scalar fields with individually steep exponential potentials cooperate through cosmic expansion to produce inflation, and what scaling attractor and curvature-perturbation spectrum result when their slopes differ?

sources.title: Rejuvenating the hope of a swampland consistent inflated multiverse with tachyonic inflation in the high-energy RS-II braneworld

evidence.text: The reviewed problem is whether inflation can simultaneously produce sufficient expansion and acceptable perturbations while obeying conjectural limits on scalar displacement, potential derivatives and horizon-entropy loss.

sources.title: Euclidean wormholes, baby universes, and their impact on particle physics and cosmology

evidence.text: Can a periodic scalar support a smooth inflationary potential over a canonical distance exceeding M_P while remaining insensitive to higher-dimension operators? The benchmark uses a protected perturbative shift symmetry and a dominant nonperturbative first harmonic.

sources.title: Seed models in scalar field cosmology

evidence.text: Can extrema of scalar-field variation restrict and relate canonical single-field Einstein-gravity cosmologies, test their inflationary predictions, and organize their post-inflationary evolution into seed models for modified gravity?

sources.title: Swampland conjecture and inflation model from brane perspective

evidence.text: How does a quadratic energy-density correction to the expansion rate alter single-field inflation? The parameter Λ sets the crossover between the ordinary Friedmann behavior and the brane-dominated regime.

sources.title: Constraints on the spectral index for the inflation models in string landscape

evidence.text: Can a scalar drive inflation through a canonical field excursion exceeding the Planck scale while remaining in the string landscape? The paper proposes a negative answer and tests selected constructions.

sources.title: Fat inflatons, large turns and the $\eta$-problem

evidence.text: The setting tests which properties of a scalar potential and its trajectory are required for inflation without presupposing a light potential-Hessian eigenvalue.

sources.title: Topological Eternal Hilltop Inflation and the Swampland Criteria

evidence.text: The baseline asks when Hubble damping allows a scalar to roll slowly and how its potential predicts inflationary observables. The expansion law links potential derivatives to the dynamical conditions for slow roll.

sources.title: Primordial Black Holes and the String Swampland

evidence.text: The inflationary setting translates restrictions on a scalar potential into restrictions on primordial perturbations through canonical single-field slow-roll relations.

sources.title: A note on Inflation and the Swampland

evidence.text: Can a canonical potential with an exponentially flat positive plateau produce many e-folds without a large field excursion? The example has height V0 and a positive dimensionless steepness parameter q.

sources.title: Constraints on the spectral index for the inflation models in string landscape

evidence.text: Can landscape inflation evade the small-tensor conclusion by using a different mechanism? The paper identifies successive vacuum tunnelling as an alternative outside its slow-roll field-budget calculation.

sources.title: Swampland implications of GW170817-compatible Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity

evidence.text: How much scalar motion does tensor production require over an inflationary interval, and can that motion remain below an order-one distance bound?

sources.title: A Tip for Landscape Riders: Multi-Field Inflation Can Fulfill the Swampland Distance Conjecture

evidence.text: The setting describes inflation driven by several scalar coordinates whose kinetic terms define a curved field space. Background trajectories and distances depend on this metric, while perturbations probe both its curvature and the potential.

sources.title: Constraints on the spectral index for the inflation models in string landscape

evidence.text: Can a Wilson-line scalar acquire a large canonical normalization scale through a small four-dimensional gauge coupling? The extranatural-inflation example makes this possibility explicit before gravitational consistency restrictions are applied.
